title: Expanding and decorating the shop
summary: Your shop is something you build up over time: the game separates expansion, furniture, upgrades, shop customisation and decoration into their own systems.
body: Expansion is its own screen and its own step, so growing the building is a distinct decision from buying stock.
Furniture is bought through a separate screen, which is why placing a shelf and expanding the shop are not the same action.
Upgrades are a defined set of choices, and decoration has its own data and panel, so how the shop looks is tracked separately from what it can do.

The decoration panel is built from states rather than one button. It shows a centred name and a line for whether you already own the piece, then separate button groups for buying it, for having bought it, for placing it, for equipping it and for changing it, with a locked background and an animation for each state.

A piece of decoration carries its own data. It has a main name and optional replacement names, a flag for a bar, a main texture with a roughness map and a normal map, a colour and a smoothness, which is why a piece looks like itself rather than like a generic shape.
What this entry does not tell you: costs, what each expansion unlocks or how decoration affects customers. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Expanding the shop has its own interface screen.
Furniture is purchased through a separate screen.
Shop customisation and decoration are tracked as their own data.
The build names arrow signs for entering and exiting, in several lettered variants.
Shop purchases are grouped into defined kinds.
The decoration panel shows a centred name and whether the piece is already owned.
It keeps separate button groups for buying, having bought, placing, equipping and changing a piece, with a locked background and an animation for each state.
facts.evidence: identifiers: m_BuyBtnGrp, m_BoughtBtnGrp, m_PlaceBtnGrp, m_EquippedBtnGrp, m_EquippedBtnGrpB, m_ChangeBtnGrp, m_ChangeBtnGrpB, m_ChangeBtnGrpB_Locked, m_LockedBG, m_BuyBtnAnim, m_BoughtBtnAnim, m_EquippedBtnAnim, m_EquippedBtnAnimB

facts.claim: A decoration piece carries a main name, optional replacement names, a bar flag, a main texture with a roughness map and a normal map, a colour and a smoothness.
facts.evidence: identifiers: mainNameText, replaceNameXXXText, replaceNameYYYText, showBar, mainTexture, roughnessMap, normalMap, color, smoothness

facts.claim: The signs go beyond arrows: the build names an empty sign with a material of its own, a no-entry sign and a sign for a closed counter.
facts.evidence: asset names: EmptySignModel, MAT_EmptySign, MAT_NoEntrySign, MAT_CounterClosedSign

facts.claim: The arrow signs are things you can interact with, and the build also names a plain arrow sign.
The build also names an open-sign material, a close-sign mesh and a sign for a closed warehouse room.
Card displays are named in sizes of their own, including a three-by-two wall and a big and a small electronic model.
Monster statues are shipped as a set of their own, with dragons for earth, fire, thunder and water and a bear, a golem and a piggy among them, some with shiny versions.
facts.evidence: asset names: Interactable_MonsterStatue_DragonEarth, Interactable_MonsterStatue_DragonFire, Interactable_MonsterStatue_DragonThunder, Interactable_MonsterStatue_DragonWater, Interactable_MonsterStatue_Bear, Interactable_MonsterStatue_GolemA, Interactable_MonsterStatue_ShinyGolemA, Interactable_MonsterStatue_PiggyA

facts.claim: A weapons closet is shipped as a fitting of its own, with a glass and a metal version and a second variant beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Weapons closet glass, Weapons closet metal, weapons closet B

facts.claim: The shop's own surfaces are named as well: a wall, a wall bar and a floor, each with a default sheet.
facts.evidence: asset names: wall_Default, wallBar_Default R, floor_Default

facts.claim: The floor carries a normal sheet beside its default one.
The arrow signs are drawn from an atlas of exit and enter boards, in lettered variants and several colours, with a running-figure exit sign among them.
The open and closed signs, and the no-entry board with its welcome counterpart, are each drawn from a single sheet of the build's own, as is the counter-closed sign.
The water dragon carries a texture, a material and a ghost version of its own, with its attack pose named beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_DragonWater, MAT_WaterDragon, Ghost_DragonWater, WaterDragon_AtkPose

facts.claim: A water diorama and a water eye are named with their own sheets.
A diorama is carried for the other elements as well: earth, fire and wind are named beside the water one.
